name: OpenVibe.Quest
description: OpenVibe.Quest is the network's shared quest log: real things you do on OpenVibe sites — going live, following someone, starting a thread, chatting, playing, improving a wiki page — complete quests that pay badges, and OpenCoins once they are switched on. Quest counts only the events the sites already report. Next: OpenCoins rewards, quests streamers and communities write, and quests for OpenVibe.Games.

pillars.title: One log, many sites
pillars.text: Streams, threads, chat messages, wiki edits and games: one quest log across eight OpenVibe sites.

pillars.title: Only what really happened
pillars.text: Quest runs nothing of its own; it listens to what the sites already report.

pillars.title: Rewards are badges
pillars.text: A badge on your profile across the network, and OpenCoins: loyalty points, never money.

pillars.title: Built for games
pillars.text: OpenVibe.Games reports to it like every other site, so play counts too.

faq.question: How does Quest know what I did?
faq.answer: The OpenVibe sites already report events such as a stream starting or a thread being posted. Quest counts the ones its quests name, for the person each event names, and nothing else: no page views, no clicks, nothing you wrote.

faq.question: What do quests pay?
faq.answer: A badge for each completed quest, shown on your profile across the network. OpenCoins rewards are built and switch on soon.

faq.question: Are OpenCoins money?
faq.answer: No. OpenCoins are loyalty points for the OpenVibe network. They are never money, and Quest never pays in Vibes.

faq.question: Can my community make its own quests?
faq.answer: Not yet: community quests need moderation tools first. The quest log and its API are already built for them.

keywords: openvibe quest, quests, achievements, rewards, gamification, streamer quests
